description: Software Development for Monitoring Astronauts' Health During Space Missions
summary:
SpaceX Health Tracker is a software solution for daily health monitoring of astronauts during long space missions.

What we developed. We researched the five main spaceflight hazards: radiation, microgravity, isolation, closed environment and distance from Earth. Then we built a working demo: a Python monitoring core and a pixel-style web dashboard. Astronauts record sleep, exercise, heart rate, stress and nutrition, and write a short well-being diary.

How it solves the task. The software compares the data with normal ranges and gives a simple traffic-light status: green (normal), yellow (attention) or red (critical). It also finds early negative trends, such as a week of bad sleep, even when today’s numbers still look normal. Game elements (points, levels and daily challenges) keep the crew motivated during isolation.

Why it is important. Space changes the body slowly: bones, muscles, heart, vision, sleep and mood. Astronauts may not notice this alone, and doctors on Earth are far away. Early warnings help the crew react in time and prevent a critical health condition.
details:
Project details

What it does and how it works. SpaceX Health Tracker is software for daily monitoring of astronauts' physical and mental health on long missions, for example to the Moon or Mars. Every day the astronaut enters sleep hours, exercise minutes, resting heart rate, stress level, meals and vitamins. In the real system, wearable sensors would provide most of this data. The astronaut also writes a short well-being diary.

A rules engine compares the data with normal ranges and gives a traffic-light status:

  • Green: normal, continue the plan.
  • Yellow: attention. An indicator is outside the norm, or it gets worse for several days. Adjust the daily plan.
  • Red: critical. Act at once and contact doctors on Earth.

The engine also looks for trends. It warns about bad sleep for several days in a row, a falling sleep trend even if today's number is still normal, and several indicators getting worse together. It scans the diary for warning words such as "blurry vision" or "tired". A weekly sleep graph shows the trend clearly.

Benefits. Space changes the body slowly, so astronauts may not notice a problem. Our tool gives the crew and doctors on Earth fast, simple and clear information. It finds problems early, supports daily healthy habits (exercise, food, sleep) and keeps motivation high during isolation.

Expected impact. Early warnings help the crew react before a health problem becomes critical. This can protect bones, muscles, heart, vision, sleep and mood. The data also helps doctors to improve future missions. The same idea can be used in other isolated places, such as polar stations or analog missions on Earth.

Tools and technologies. We used Python (standard library only) for the monitoring core, SQLite for data storage, a small JSON API (http.server) and unittest for tests. The web demo is built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript (canvas graphics). The presentation was made in a slide editor. In this demo we use simulated data. No real hardware was used, but the design supports wearable sensors.

Creativity. We combined three ideas: a simple traffic light that anyone understands in a second, early trend detection that warns before the numbers are dangerous, and gamification (points, levels, achievements and daily challenges) so that health tracking is not boring. The pixel-game style of the logo and interface makes the system friendly and memorable.

Factors we considered.

  • The five spaceflight hazards and their effect on the body: bone and muscle loss, heart and vision changes (SANS), sleep problems, stress and poor nutrition.
  • Isolation and limited help from Earth. The software is simple, runs without internet and keeps data local.
  • Safety. All limits in the demo are examples. Real limits must be set by medical experts.
  • Usability. The interface is clear, short and fast to use, because the crew has little free time.
  • Flexibility. All thresholds are in one configuration file, so doctors can change them easily.
